- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots and forecasts too high for next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +10–15% above peak or align with 1–2 prior-day mean.
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., >0.5) after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; increase forecast slope or add 2–3% upward bias to early days of rebound.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early days of a 30-day forecast (e.g., day 1–5), especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — adjust downward bias by 1–2% for first 3 days.
- When sentiment is flat (0.0–0.5) for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to overpredict mean reversion — reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is positive but price is falling (e.g., +0.6 but price dropping), model often misreads trend — forecast should reflect slight downward bias or pause in momentum.
- Model frequently overestimates volatility in early forecast days when sentiment is volatile — smooth out first 3–5 days’ forecast by averaging with prior 3-day moving average.
